statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n stone heights. A frog starts on stone 0 and must reach stone n-1, jumping 1 or 2 stones ahead; a jump costs the absolute height difference. Print the minimum total energy. State: f(i) is the cheapest way to stand on stone i. Transition: arrive from i-1 or i-2, paying the respective difference - take the cheaper. Roll two variables; f(0) is 0.

example.why: The route 0 to 1 to 3 pays 10 plus 10; every route that touches the tall stone pays 40.

hint: Guard the i-2 case at i = 1 - there is no stone -1 to arrive from.
mistake: Greedy hopping to the closer height; a pricey hop now can dodge two pricey hops later.
